source.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַֽחֲרֵי֙ מ֣וֹת שָׁא֔וּל וְדָוִ֣ד שָׁ֔ב מֵהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת־הָעֲמָלֵ֑ק וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב דָּוִ֛ד בְּצִקְלָ֖ג יָמִ֥ים שְׁנָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was after [the] death of Saul, and David had returned from striking the Amalekites, and stayed David in Ziklag days two.

en.L: And it happened after the death of Saul, when David had returned from striking down the Amalekites, that David stayed in Ziklag two days.
en.B: After the death of Saul, when David had come back from defeating the Amalekites, David stayed in Ziklag for two days.
en.R: Saul was now dead. David had come back from beating the Amalekites in battle, and he stayed in the town of Ziklag for two days.

es.L: Y sucedió después de la muerte de Saúl, cuando David había vuelto de herir a los amalecitas, que David se quedó en Siclag dos días.
es.B: Después de la muerte de Saúl, cuando David había regresado de derrotar a los amalecitas, David se quedó dos días en Siclag.
es.R: Saúl ya había muerto. David había vuelto de vencer en batalla a los amalecitas, y se quedó dos días en el pueblo de Siclag.

fr.L: Et il arriva, après la mort de Saül, quand David fut revenu de frapper les Amalécites, que David resta à Tsiqlag deux jours.
fr.B: Après la mort de Saül, quand David fut revenu de sa victoire sur les Amalécites, il resta deux jours à Tsiqlag.
fr.R: Saül était mort. David était revenu après avoir battu les Amalécites, et il est resté deux jours dans la ville de Tsiqlag.

sw.L: Ikawa baada ya kifo cha Sauli, Daudi alipokuwa amerudi kutoka kuwapiga Waamaleki, Daudi akakaa Siklagi siku mbili.
sw.B: Baada ya kifo cha Sauli, Daudi alipokuwa amerudi kutoka kuwashinda Waamaleki, alikaa Siklagi kwa siku mbili.
sw.R: Sauli alikuwa amekwisha kufa. Daudi alikuwa amerudi kutoka vitani, ambako aliwashinda Waamaleki, naye akakaa katika mji wa Siklagi kwa siku mbili.

vi.L: Sau khi Sau-lơ chết, khi Đa-vít đã trở về từ cuộc đánh giết người A-ma-léc, thì Đa-vít ở lại Xiếc-lác hai ngày.
vi.B: Sau khi Sau-lơ chết, Đa-vít đánh bại người A-ma-léc trở về và ở lại Xiếc-lác hai ngày.
vi.R: Lúc ấy Sau-lơ đã chết. Đa-vít vừa đánh thắng người A-ma-léc trở về, và ông ở lại thị trấn Xiếc-lác hai ngày.

ko.L: 사울이 죽은 뒤의 일이다. 다윗이 아말렉 사람들을 쳐부수고 돌아와서, 다윗이 시글락에서 이틀 동안 머물렀다.
ko.B: 사울이 죽은 뒤, 다윗은 아말렉 사람들을 쳐부수고 돌아와 시글락에서 이틀 동안 머물렀다.
ko.R: 사울은 이미 죽었다. 다윗은 아말렉 사람들과 싸워 이기고 돌아와서, 시글락 성에서 이틀 동안 머물렀다.

pt.L: E aconteceu, depois da morte de Saul, quando Davi tinha voltado de ferir os amalequitas, que Davi ficou em Ziclague dois dias.
pt.B: Depois da morte de Saul, quando Davi tinha voltado da vitória sobre os amalequitas, Davi ficou dois dias em Ziclague.
pt.R: Saul já estava morto. Davi tinha voltado depois de vencer os amalequitas na batalha e ficou dois dias na cidade de Ziclague.

am.B: ሳኦል ከሞተ በኋላ፣ ዳዊት አማሌቃውያንን ድል አድርጎ ተመልሶ በጺቅላግ ሁለት ቀን ቆየ።
am.R: ሳኦል ሞቶ ነበር። ዳዊት አማሌቃውያንን በጦርነት አሸንፎ ተመልሶ ነበር፤ በጺቅላግ ከተማም ሁለት ቀን ቆየ።

hi.L: और शाऊल की मृत्यु के बाद ऐसा हुआ, जब दाऊद अमालेकियों को मारकर लौट आया था, कि दाऊद सिकलग में दो दिन रहा।
hi.B: शाऊल की मृत्यु के बाद, जब दाऊद अमालेकियों को हराकर लौट आया था, तब दाऊद दो दिन सिकलग में रहा।
hi.R: अब शाऊल मर चुका था। दाऊद अमालेकियों को युद्ध में हराकर लौट आया था, और वह सिकलग नगर में दो दिन रहा।

ru.L: И было после смерти Саула: Давид вернулся, поразив амаликитян, и пробыл Давид в Секелаге два дня.
ru.B: После смерти Саула, когда Давид вернулся после победы над амаликитянами, он пробыл в Секелаге два дня.
ru.R: Саул был уже мёртв. Давид вернулся после того, как разбил амаликитян в битве, и два дня пробыл в городе Секелаге.

ja.L: そして、サウルが死んだ後のことである。ダビデはアマレク人を打ち倒して戻っていて、ダビデはツィクラグに二日間とどまった。
ja.B: サウルが死んだ後、ダビデはアマレク人を打ち破って戻り、ツィクラグに二日間とどまった。
ja.R: サウルは、もう死んでいました。ダビデはアマレク人との戦いに勝って戻り、ツィクラグの町に二日間とどまっていました。

uk.L: І сталося після смерті Саула, коли Давид повернувся, побивши амаликитян, Давид пробув у Ціклазі два дні.
uk.B: Після Саулової смерті, коли Давид повернувся з перемоги над амаликитянами, він пробув у Ціклазі два дні.
uk.R: Саул уже був мертвий. Давид повернувся після перемоги над амаликитянами й пробув у місті Ціклаг два дні.

decisions.choice: the setting: just after Saul's death in battle on Mount Gilboa (1 Samuel 31)
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew tradition 1 and 2 Samuel were a single book; it was divided into two later. This book picks up directly where 1 Samuel ends. Saul and three of his sons, Jonathan among them, died when the Philistines defeated Israel on Mount Gilboa (1 Samuel 31:1-6). The opening words echo the start of Joshua ("after the death of Moses", Joshua 1:1) and Judges ("after the death of Joshua", Judges 1:1): a leader's death closes one stage of Israel's story and opens the next.

decisions.choice: David's return from striking the Amalekites: the rescue of Ziklag (1 Samuel 30)
decisions.reason: While Saul was fighting the Philistines, David was pursuing the Amalekite raiders who had burned Ziklag and taken its families captive. He struck them down and brought everyone back (1 Samuel 30:1-20). The two battles happened at about the same time, far apart: Saul's in the north, David's in the south.

decisions.choice: Ziklag: the town in the south that the Philistine king Achish gave David
decisions.reason: Achish king of Gath gave David Ziklag while David was living among the Philistines to escape Saul (1 Samuel 27:6). It was the home of David and his men until he moved to Hebron (2:1-3).

decisions.choice: Saul was now dead. ... in the town of Ziklag
decisions.reason: Readable turns the time clause into a short sentence of its own and says that Ziklag was a town.

decisions.choice: passé simple for the narrative at Literal and Balanced ("il arriva", "resta"); passé composé at Readable ("il est resté"); speech in the tenses of speech at every level, including the stories people tell inside it
decisions.reason: For the whole of 2 Samuel, as the French style guide and the Samuel terms note set: the passé simple is the tense of written French narrative, the passé composé the tense of spoken French and of the plain Readable level. The Amalekite's account (verses 6-10) and David's lament (19-27) are speech, so they use the passé composé at every level.

decisions.choice: "Saúl", "David", "los amalecitas", "Siclag"
decisions.reason: For the whole of 2 Samuel, the names follow the Samuel terms note and the Spanish Pentateuch and Psalm titles: "Saúl", "Jonatán", "los amalecitas", "Siclag", "los filisteos", "Gat". Narrative is in the preterite at every level, as the Pentateuch note sets for Spanish.

decisions.choice: Sauli alikuwa amekwisha kufa ... katika mji wa Siklagi
decisions.reason: As the English Readable, the time clause becomes its own short sentence, and Ziklag is called a town ("mji").

decisions.choice: "Sau-lơ", "Đa-vít", "Xiếc-lác", "người A-ma-léc"
decisions.reason: The names keep the forms of the Samuel terms note and the Vietnamese New Testament; David is "ông" in the narration, as Genesis narrates of its heads of households.

decisions.choice: The narrative of 2 Samuel is told in the plain written style (-었다), with the honorific -시- only for God
decisions.reason: As the Korean style guide and the Samuel terms note set for narrative; the earlier Korean books (Genesis) are told the same way.

decisions.choice: Saul, Davi, os amalequitas, Ziclague; the names of 1 Samuel
decisions.reason: For the whole book: 2 Samuel continues 1 Samuel (m1), so its Portuguese keeps 1 Samuel's names and terms: Davi, Saul, Jônatas, Mical, Abner filho de Ner, Joabe, Abisai, Asael, Jabes-Gileade, Ziclague (1 Samuel 27:6), Gilboa, os amalequitas, os filisteus, Gate, Ascalom; round numbers in words ("seiscentos", "vinte mil") and long non-round counts in figures, as style section 5. Later chapters follow these forms without a new decision.

decisions.choice: For the whole of 2 Samuel: the divine name is "{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}" at every level, with the whole inflected word in each option ("{{divine_name:የእግዚአብሔር|የያህዌ}}"); "YHWH Tsevaot" ("the LORD of Armies", from 5:10) is "{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ጸባኦት" at Literal and "የሠራዊት አምላክ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}" at Balanced and Readable; "the LORD God of Armies" (5:10) is "{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} የሠራዊት አምላክ" at Balanced and Readable and "{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} የጸባኦት አምላክ" at Literal; Elohim standing alone for the one God is "እግዚአብሔር" ("the ark of God" "የእግዚአብሔር ታቦት"), and "my God, your God, the God of Israel" is "አምላኬ", "አምላክህ", "የእስራኤል አምላክ"; Adonai YHWH (7:18-29) is "ጌታ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}". "The LORD's anointed" is "{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} የቀባው" (Readable "{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} የቀባው ንጉሥ").
alternatives: "የሠራዊት ጌታ" for YHWH Tsevaot at every level
decisions.reason: As in Genesis to Deuteronomy and the other books from Joshua to 2 Samuel, so that the books read as one. "ጸባኦት" is the Hebrew word for "armies" (hosts), kept as part of the title at Literal as the Ethiopian Bible tradition knows it; Balanced and Readable say what it means, "the God of armies" ("የሠራዊት አምላክ"), the armies of heaven and of Israel that the LORD commands. "ጌታ" is kept for Adonai.

decisions.choice: Forms of address for 2 Samuel: subjects, servants and soldiers speak to a king (David, Ish-bosheth) with "እርስዎ" and "ጌታዬ ንጉሥ", and where the Hebrew uses the courtly third person they call themselves "ባሪያዎ" (Literal) / "አገልጋይዎ" (Balanced, Readable), and "the LORD your God" said to a king is "አምላክዎ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}"; a king's own sons, as family, say "አንተ" to him; a king speaks down with "አንተ" / "እናንተ"; equals and fellow commanders (Abner and Joab, Abner and Asahel) say "አንተ"; the prophet Nathan, bringing God's word, says "አንተ" to David, and David prays to God with "አንተ" (chapter 7). Names follow the Joshua to 2 Samuel terms list (ኢዮአብ, አቢሳ, አሣሄል, አበኔር, ኢያቡስቴ, ሜምፊቦስቴ, ሜልኮል, ናታን).
decisions.reason: Amharic must choose a form of address that the Hebrew does not mark; keeping one choice for each pair of speakers through the book keeps the relationships steady. A prophet speaking for God stands above the king in that moment, as Moses before Pharaoh.

decisions.choice: Saul and David with plain third-person forms ("शाऊल मर चुका था", "वह रहा")
decisions.reason: As in 1 Samuel in this translation, the narrator speaks of Saul, David and the other people of the story with plain singular forms; only God takes the honorific plural. This holds for the whole of 2 Samuel, David as king included.

decisions.choice: "Саул", "Давид", "амаликитяне", "Секелаг"
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel continues 1 Samuel directly, and the Russian keeps 1 Samuel's forms of names, terms and address throughout the book (Секелаг as at 1 Samuel 27:6, амаликитяне as at 27:8).

decisions.choice: Narration plain (だ・である) at Literal and Balanced, です・ます at Readable; light respect forms for God only, as 1 Samuel and Judges
alternatives: です・ます at every level
decisions.reason: The book-wide register of the Japanese Old Testament narrative books; settled once here for 2 Samuel.

decisions.choice: "アマレク人", "ツィクラグ" (Readable "ツィクラグの町")
decisions.reason: The forms used in Joshua 15:31 and 1 Samuel; Readable names the town as the English does.

decisions.choice: The divine name is "{{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}", inflected inside each option, at every level of the book; "Господь" in ordinary letters is kept for Adonai
decisions.reason: The capitals mirror the English "the LORD" and keep the name apart from Adonai, as the shared Old Testament note settles; the setting shows the name itself.

decisions.choice: Names for the whole book keep the forms of the 1 Samuel draft ("Саул", "амаликитяни", "Ціклаг", "Гілбоа", "Йонатан", "Авнер", "Йоав", "Авішай", "Церуя") and of the Kings draft for those who go on into 1 Kings ("Адонія", "Садок", "Авіятар", "Беная", "Натан", "Вірсавія", "Шимей", "Мефівошет", "Барзіллай", "Ахітофел")
decisions.reason: One form for each name through Samuel and Kings; the names that are not in the shared table are listed in the pull request.

decisions.choice: Narrative in the perfective past; the "і... і..." chain kept at Literal, smoothed at Balanced, short sentences at Readable; "мій пане, царю" and "твій раб" in courtly speech
decisions.reason: The same register as the 1 Samuel draft and the shared Old Testament note.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗י וְהִנֵּה֩ אִ֨ישׁ בָּ֤א מִן־הַֽמַּחֲנֶה֙ מֵעִ֣ם שָׁא֔וּל וּבְגָדָ֣יו קְרֻעִ֔ים וַאֲדָמָ֖ה עַל־רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַיְהִי֙ בְּבֹא֣וֹ אֶל־דָּוִ֔ד וַיִּפֹּ֥ל אַ֖רְצָה וַיִּשְׁתָּֽחוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was on the day the third, and look, a man coming from the camp, from with Saul, and his garments torn, and earth on his head; and it was when he came to David, and he fell to [the] ground and bowed down.

en.L: And it happened on the third day, and look, a man came from the camp, from Saul, with his clothes torn and earth on his head. And when he came to David, he fell to the ground and bowed down.
en.B: On the third day a man arrived from Saul's camp. His clothes were torn, and there was dirt on his head. When he came to David, he threw himself to the ground and bowed low.
en.R: On the third day a man came from Saul's army camp. His clothes were torn, and there was dirt on his head to show his sorrow. When he came to David, he bowed down with his face to the ground.

es.L: Y sucedió al tercer día, y he aquí que un hombre vino del campamento, de con Saúl, con la ropa rasgada y tierra sobre la cabeza. Y cuando llegó a David, cayó a tierra y se postró.
es.B: Al tercer día llegó un hombre del campamento de Saúl. Traía la ropa rasgada y tierra sobre la cabeza. Cuando llegó ante David, se echó al suelo y se inclinó profundamente.
es.R: Al tercer día llegó un hombre del campamento del ejército de Saúl. Tenía la ropa rasgada y tierra en la cabeza en señal de dolor. Cuando llegó ante David, se inclinó con el rostro en tierra.

fr.L: Et il arriva le troisième jour, et voici, un homme vint du camp, d’auprès de Saül, les vêtements déchirés et de la terre sur la tête. Et quand il arriva auprès de David, il tomba à terre et se prosterna.
fr.B: Le troisième jour, un homme arriva du camp de Saül. Ses vêtements étaient déchirés et il avait de la terre sur la tête. Quand il parvint auprès de David, il se jeta à terre et se prosterna.
fr.R: Le troisième jour, un homme est arrivé du camp de l’armée de Saül. Ses vêtements étaient déchirés et il avait de la terre sur la tête pour montrer son chagrin. Quand il est arrivé devant David, il s’est incliné, le visage contre le sol.

sw.L: Ikawa siku ya tatu, na tazama, mtu akaja kutoka kambini, kutoka kwa Sauli, mavazi yake yameraruliwa na udongo juu ya kichwa chake. Ikawa alipofika kwa Daudi, akaanguka chini akasujudu.
sw.B: Siku ya tatu mtu mmoja alifika kutoka kambi ya Sauli. Mavazi yake yalikuwa yameraruka, na kichwani mwake palikuwa na mavumbi. Alipomfikia Daudi, alijitupa chini, akasujudu.
sw.R: Siku ya tatu mtu mmoja alikuja kutoka kambi ya jeshi la Sauli. Nguo zake zilikuwa zimeraruka, na kichwani alikuwa na mavumbi kuonyesha huzuni yake. Alipomfikia Daudi, aliinama mpaka uso wake ukagusa ardhi.

vi.L: Đến ngày thứ ba, kìa, có một người từ trại quân, từ chỗ Sau-lơ đến, áo xống xé rách, đầu đầy đất. Khi đến gặp Đa-vít, người ấy sấp mình xuống đất và lạy.
vi.B: Đến ngày thứ ba, có một người từ trại quân của Sau-lơ đến. Áo người ấy rách, đầu dính đầy đất. Khi đến trước mặt Đa-vít, người ấy sấp mình xuống đất mà lạy.
vi.R: Đến ngày thứ ba, có một người từ trại quân của Sau-lơ đến. Áo người ấy bị xé rách, trên đầu có đất để tỏ lòng buồn rầu. Khi đến gặp Đa-vít, người ấy cúi sấp mặt xuống đất.

ko.L: 셋째 날이 되었는데, 보라, 한 사람이 진영에서, 사울에게서 왔다. 그의 옷은 찢어졌고 그의 머리에는 흙이 있었다. 그가 다윗에게 왔을 때, 땅에 엎드려 절했다.
ko.B: 사흘째 되는 날, 한 사람이 사울의 진영에서 왔다. 그는 옷이 찢어지고 머리에 흙을 뒤집어쓰고 있었다. 그는 다윗에게 와서 땅에 엎드려 절했다.
ko.R: 사흘째 되는 날, 한 남자가 사울의 군대 진영에서 왔다. 그는 옷이 찢어져 있었고, 슬픔을 나타내려고 머리에 흙을 뒤집어쓰고 있었다. 그는 다윗 앞에 와서 얼굴을 땅에 대고 절했다.

pt.L: E aconteceu no terceiro dia, e eis que um homem veio do acampamento, de junto de Saul, com as suas roupas rasgadas e terra sobre a sua cabeça. E, quando ele chegou a Davi, caiu por terra e se prostrou.
pt.B: No terceiro dia, chegou um homem do acampamento de Saul. Estava com as roupas rasgadas e com terra na cabeça. Quando chegou diante de Davi, ele se lançou ao chão e se prostrou.
pt.R: No terceiro dia, chegou um homem que vinha do acampamento do exército de Saul. As roupas dele estavam rasgadas, e ele tinha terra na cabeça, para mostrar a sua tristeza. Quando chegou perto de Davi, ele se curvou com o rosto no chão.

am.L: በሦስተኛውም ቀን እነሆ፣ ልብሱ የተቀደደ፣ በራሱም ላይ ትቢያ ያለበት አንድ ሰው ከሰፈሩ፣ ከሳኦል ዘንድ መጣ። ወደ ዳዊትም በመጣ ጊዜ በምድር ላይ ወድቆ ሰገደ።
am.B: በሦስተኛው ቀን አንድ ሰው ከሳኦል ሰፈር መጣ። ልብሱ ተቀድዶ፣ በራሱም ላይ ትቢያ ነስንሶ ነበር። ወደ ዳዊትም በደረሰ ጊዜ በምድር ላይ ተደፍቶ እጅ ነሣ።
am.R: በሦስተኛው ቀን አንድ ሰው ከሳኦል የጦር ሰፈር መጣ። ሐዘኑን ለማሳየት ልብሱን ቀድዶ በራሱ ላይ አፈር ነስንሶ ነበር። ወደ ዳዊትም በመጣ ጊዜ በግንባሩ ተደፍቶ ሰገደ።

hi.L: और तीसरे दिन ऐसा हुआ, कि देखो, एक पुरुष छावनी से, शाऊल के पास से, आया; उसके वस्त्र फटे हुए थे और उसके सिर पर मिट्टी थी। और जब वह दाऊद के पास आया, तो वह भूमि पर गिरा और उसने दंडवत किया।
hi.B: तीसरे दिन शाऊल की छावनी से एक पुरुष आया। उसके वस्त्र फटे हुए थे, और उसके सिर पर धूल पड़ी थी। जब वह दाऊद के पास पहुँचा, तो उसने भूमि पर गिरकर दंडवत किया।
hi.R: तीसरे दिन शाऊल की सेना की छावनी से एक आदमी आया। उसके कपड़े फटे हुए थे, और अपना दुख दिखाने के लिए उसने सिर पर धूल डाल रखी थी। जब वह दाऊद के पास आया, तो उसने भूमि पर मुँह के बल झुककर उसे प्रणाम किया।

ru.L: И было на третий день: и вот, человек пришёл из стана, от Саула, и одежда его разорвана, и земля на его голове. И было, когда он пришёл к Давиду, пал он на землю и поклонился.
ru.B: На третий день из лагеря Саула пришёл человек. Одежда на нём была разорвана, а на голове была земля. Подойдя к Давиду, он бросился на землю и низко поклонился.
ru.R: На третий день из военного лагеря Саула пришёл человек. Его одежда была разорвана, а голова посыпана землёй в знак горя. Подойдя к Давиду, он поклонился ему до земли.

ja.L: そして三日目のことであった。なんと、一人の男が陣営から、サウルのもとから来た。その衣は裂け、頭には土があった。そして彼はダビデのもとに来ると、地に倒れ伏して身をかがめた。
ja.B: 三日目に、一人の男がサウルの陣営からやって来た。衣は裂け、頭には土をかぶっていた。彼はダビデのところに来ると、地に身を投げ出して深く礼をした。
ja.R: 三日目に、サウルの軍の陣営から一人の男がやって来ました。その人の服は裂け、頭には土がかかっていました。悲しみを表すためです。男はダビデのところに来ると、顔を地面につけてひれ伏しました。

uk.L: І сталося третього дня, і ось чоловік прийшов з табору, від Саула, з роздертим одягом і землею на голові. І сталося, коли він прийшов до Давида, то впав на землю й поклонився.
uk.B: Третього дня з Саулового табору прийшов чоловік. Його одяг був роздертий, а на голові була земля. Прийшовши до Давида, він упав на землю й низько вклонився.
uk.R: Третього дня з Саулового військового табору прийшов чоловік. Його одяг був роздертий, а на голові була земля на знак горя. Прийшовши до Давида, він уклонився обличчям до землі.

decisions.choice: torn clothes and earth on the head: signs of mourning
decisions.reason: People tore their clothes and put dust or earth on their heads at news of death or disaster. A runner from the battle at Aphek came to Shiloh looking just the same (1 Samuel 4:12), so David can see at once that the man brings bad news.

decisions.choice: fell to the ground and bowed down: deep respect, the honor given to a ruler
decisions.reason: Bowing to the ground was how one honored a king or a great man (1 Samuel 24:9; 25:23). The man comes from Saul's camp and treats David as if he were already king; in verse 10 he calls him "my lord".

decisions.choice: the third day: counted from David's return to Ziklag
decisions.reason: Verse 1 says David had been in Ziklag two days; the man arrives on the next day.

decisions.choice: to show his sorrow
decisions.reason: Readable adds what the torn clothes and the dirt meant (m1), as at 1 Samuel 4:12.

decisions.choice: "he aquí que"
decisions.reason: In narrative the Literal level renders the Hebrew "look" with "he aquí", as the Spanish terms set for narrative; "mira" is kept for speech.

decisions.choice: kuonyesha huzuni yake
decisions.reason: Readable adds what the torn clothes and the dust meant, as the English Readable does ("to show his sorrow").

decisions.choice: "슬픔을 나타내려고" (to show his sorrow) added at Readable
decisions.reason: As the English Readable: Korean readers may not know torn clothes and earth on the head as signs of mourning.

decisions.choice: "दंडवत किया" (L, B); "मुँह के बल झुककर प्रणाम किया" (R)
decisions.reason: "दंडवत" is the Hindi word for lying face down before someone in homage, the respect given to a ruler (meaning m2); Readable describes the gesture in plain words.

decisions.choice: "стан" (Literal); "лагерь" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Samuel (4:1): Literal keeps the older word for an army camp, the other levels the everyday one.

decisions.choice: "なんと" for hinneh in the narration
decisions.reason: As in Genesis: hinneh in narration is "なんと" at Literal; Balanced and Readable leave it unspoken.

decisions.choice: "深く礼をした" (B), "ひれ伏しました" (R) for bowing to a man
decisions.reason: The bow is honor given to a ruler, not worship; "礼拝する" is kept for bowing before God.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ דָּוִ֔ד אֵ֥י מִזֶּ֖ה תָּב֑וֹא וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו מִמַּחֲנֵ֥ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נִמְלָֽטְתִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him David, Where from this do you come? And he said to him, From [the] camp of Israel I have escaped.

en.L: And David said to him, "Where do you come from?" And he said to him, "I have escaped from the camp of Israel."
en.B: David asked him, "Where have you come from?" He answered, "I have escaped from the camp of Israel."
en.R: David asked him, "Where have you come from?" The man said, "I got away from Israel's army camp."

es.L: Y le dijo David: «¿De dónde vienes?». Y él le dijo: «Del campamento de Israel he escapado».
es.B: David le preguntó: «¿De dónde vienes?». Él respondió: «He escapado del campamento de Israel».
es.R: David le preguntó: «¿De dónde vienes?». El hombre contestó: «Logré escapar del campamento del ejército de Israel».

fr.L: Et David lui dit : « D’où viens-tu ? » Et il lui dit : « Je me suis échappé du camp d’Israël. »
fr.B: David lui demanda : « D’où viens-tu ? » Il répondit : « Je me suis échappé du camp d’Israël. »
fr.R: David lui a demandé : « D’où viens-tu ? » L’homme a dit : « Je me suis sauvé du camp de l’armée d’Israël. »

sw.L: Daudi akamwambia, "Unatoka wapi?" Akamwambia, "Nimetoroka kutoka kambi ya Israeli."
sw.B: Daudi akamwuliza, "Umetoka wapi?" Akajibu, "Nimetoroka kutoka kambi ya Israeli."
sw.R: Daudi akamwuliza, "Umetoka wapi?" Yule mtu akasema, "Nimeponyoka kutoka kambi ya jeshi la Israeli."

vi.L: Đa-vít hỏi người ấy: "Ngươi từ đâu đến?" Người ấy thưa: "Tôi vừa thoát khỏi trại quân Y-sơ-ra-ên."
vi.B: Đa-vít hỏi: "Ngươi từ đâu đến?" Người ấy thưa: "Tôi đã thoát ra khỏi trại quân Y-sơ-ra-ên."
vi.R: Đa-vít hỏi: "Ngươi từ đâu đến?" Người ấy đáp: "Tôi vừa chạy thoát khỏi trại quân Y-sơ-ra-ên."

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 그에게 말했다. "너는 어디에서 오느냐?" 그러자 그가 그에게 말했다. "이스라엘 진영에서 도망쳐 나왔습니다."
ko.B: 다윗이 그에게 물었다. "너는 어디에서 왔느냐?" 그가 대답했다. "이스라엘 진영에서 겨우 빠져나왔습니다."
ko.R: 다윗이 그에게 물었다. "어디에서 왔느냐?" 그 사람이 말했다. "이스라엘 군대 진영에서 살아서 도망쳐 왔습니다."

pt.L: E Davi lhe disse: "De onde você vem?" E ele lhe disse: "Do acampamento de Israel eu escapei."
pt.B: Davi lhe perguntou: "De onde você está vindo?" Ele respondeu: "Escapei do acampamento de Israel."
pt.R: Davi perguntou: "De onde você vem?" O homem disse: "Consegui fugir do acampamento do exército de Israel."

am.L: ዳዊትም፦ «ከወዴት መጣህ?» አለው። እርሱም፦ «ከእስራኤል ሰፈር አምልጬ መጣሁ» አለው።
am.B: ዳዊትም፦ «ከየት መጣህ?» ብሎ ጠየቀው። እርሱም፦ «ከእስራኤል ሰፈር አምልጬ መጣሁ» ብሎ መለሰለት።
am.R: ዳዊትም፦ «ከየት መጣህ?» ብሎ ጠየቀው። ሰውየውም፦ «ከእስራኤል ጦር ሰፈር አምልጬ መጣሁ» አለ።

hi.L: और दाऊद ने उससे कहा, "तुम कहाँ से आ रहे हो?" और उसने उससे कहा, "मैं इस्राएल की छावनी से बच निकला हूँ।"
hi.B: दाऊद ने उससे पूछा, "तुम कहाँ से आए हो?" उसने उत्तर दिया, "मैं इस्राएल की छावनी से बचकर निकला हूँ।"
hi.R: दाऊद ने उससे पूछा, "तुम कहाँ से आए हो?" उस आदमी ने कहा, "मैं इस्राएल की सेना की छावनी से बचकर भाग आया हूँ।"

ru.L: И сказал ему Давид: «Откуда ты приходишь?» И сказал он ему: «Из стана Израиля я спасся.»
ru.B: Давид спросил его: «Откуда ты пришёл?» Тот ответил: «Я спасся из израильского лагеря.»
ru.R: Давид спросил его: «Откуда ты пришёл?» Человек сказал: «Я сбежал из лагеря израильского войска.»

ja.L: そしてダビデは彼に言った。「どこから来たのか？」彼はダビデに言った。「わたしはイスラエルの陣営から逃れて来ました。」
ja.B: ダビデが彼に「どこから来たのか？」と尋ねると、彼は答えた。「イスラエルの陣営から逃げてまいりました。」
ja.R: ダビデは「どこから来たのか？」と聞きました。男は言いました。「イスラエル軍の陣営から、やっと逃げて来ました。」

uk.L: І сказав йому Давид: «Звідки ти приходиш?» І сказав він йому: «Я втік з табору Ізраїля.»
uk.B: Давид спитав його: «Звідки ти прийшов?» Той відповів: «Я втік з ізраїльського табору.»
uk.R: Давид спитав його: «Звідки ти прийшов?» Чоловік сказав: «Я втік з табору ізраїльського війська.»

decisions.choice: I have escaped: I got away alive from the defeat
decisions.reason: The verb is used of slipping away from danger with one's life (1 Samuel 19:10-12). The word already tells David that something has gone badly wrong for Israel's army.

decisions.choice: quotation marks «» with “ ” inside and ‘ ’ inside those; a question inside a quotation takes «¿...?»
decisions.reason: For the whole of 2 Samuel, as in the Spanish Pentateuch and New Testament: speech takes the Spanish angle quotes, and a speech that runs across several verses is not closed at each verse.

decisions.choice: David says "ngươi" (and "ta") to the messenger, who answers with "tôi" and "thưa"
decisions.reason: David is a leader of men speaking to a stranger of lower rank who comes to him as to a king (verse 2); the messenger speaks up to him. Kept through the scene.

decisions.choice: David speaks to the messenger in the plain style (해라체); the messenger answers in the formal polite style (합쇼체)
decisions.reason: David is the leader of an armed band and the man comes to him bowing; the Korean terms for Samuel give a superior 해라체 and an inferior 합쇼체.

decisions.choice: escapei (L, B); consegui fugir (R)
decisions.reason: "Escapar" says that he got away from danger alive (m1), which "fugir" alone, "run away", does not; Readable says it with "consegui fugir", the plain words for getting away.

decisions.choice: David says "तुम" to the messenger
decisions.reason: David speaks to a stranger of lower rank, so he uses the familiar "तुम"; the messenger, speaking to a leader, says "आप" (verse 10 Readable) and "मेरे स्वामी".

decisions.choice: David speaks plainly to the messenger; the messenger answers politely (です・ます, Balanced "まいりました")
decisions.reason: David is the leader of the band and the man comes to him as a suppliant; the register holds through the scene.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֥יו דָּוִ֛ד מֶה־הָיָ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר הַגֶּד־נָ֣א לִ֑י וַ֠יֹּאמֶר אֲשֶׁר־נָ֨ס הָעָ֜ם מִן־הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וְגַם־הַרְבֵּ֞ה נָפַ֤ל מִן־הָעָם֙ וַיָּמֻ֔תוּ וְגַ֗ם שָׁא֛וּל וִיהוֹנָתָ֥ן בְּנ֖וֹ מֵֽתוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him David, What was the word? Tell, please, to me. And he said that fled the people from the battle, and also many fell from the people and died, and also Saul and Jonathan his son died.

en.L: And David said to him, "What was the matter? Tell me, please." And he said, "The people fled from the battle, and also many of the people fell and died, and also Saul and Jonathan his son are dead."
en.B: David said to him, "What happened? Please tell me." He said, "The troops fled from the battle, and many of them fell and died. Saul and his son Jonathan are dead too."
en.R: "What happened?" David asked. "Please tell me." The man said, "The army ran away from the battle. Many of the soldiers were killed. Saul and his son Jonathan are dead too."

es.L: Y le dijo David: «¿Qué pasó? Cuéntamelo, te ruego». Y él dijo: «El pueblo huyó de la batalla, y también muchos del pueblo cayeron y murieron, y también Saúl y Jonatán su hijo han muerto».
es.B: David le dijo: «¿Qué sucedió? Por favor, cuéntamelo». Él dijo: «Las tropas huyeron de la batalla, y muchos de ellos cayeron y murieron. También han muerto Saúl y su hijo Jonatán».
es.R: «¿Qué pasó?», preguntó David. «Por favor, dímelo». El hombre respondió: «El ejército huyó de la batalla. Muchos soldados murieron. También han muerto Saúl y su hijo Jonatán».

fr.L: Et David lui dit : « Quelle a été l’affaire ? Raconte-moi, je te prie. » Et il dit : « Le peuple s’est enfui de la bataille, et aussi beaucoup du peuple sont tombés et sont morts, et aussi Saül et Jonathan son fils sont morts. »
fr.B: David lui dit : « Que s’est-il passé ? Raconte-moi, je t’en prie. » Il répondit : « Les troupes ont fui le combat, et beaucoup d’entre elles sont tombées et sont mortes. Saül et son fils Jonathan sont morts, eux aussi. »
fr.R: « Que s’est-il passé ? a demandé David. Raconte-moi, s’il te plaît. » L’homme a dit : « L’armée s’est enfuie pendant la bataille. Beaucoup de soldats ont été tués. Saül et son fils Jonathan sont morts, eux aussi. »

sw.L: Daudi akamwambia, "Jambo lilikuwa nini? Tafadhali niambie." Akasema, "Watu wamekimbia kutoka vitani, tena wengi wa watu wameanguka wakafa, tena Sauli na Yonathani mwanawe wamekufa."
sw.B: Daudi akamwambia, "Ni nini kilichotokea? Tafadhali niambie." Akasema, "Askari wamekimbia vitani, na wengi wao wameanguka wakafa. Sauli na mwanawe Yonathani nao wamekufa."
sw.R: Daudi akauliza, "Nini kimetokea? Tafadhali niambie." Yule mtu akasema, "Jeshi limekimbia vitani. Askari wengi wameuawa. Sauli na mwanawe Yonathani nao wamekufa."

vi.L: Đa-vít hỏi người ấy: "Sự việc thế nào? Hãy kể cho ta nghe." Người ấy thưa: "Quân lính đã chạy trốn khỏi trận chiến, và cũng có nhiều người trong dân đã ngã xuống và chết; Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than con trai người cũng đã chết."
vi.B: Đa-vít nói: "Việc gì đã xảy ra? Hãy kể cho ta nghe." Người ấy thưa: "Quân lính đã bỏ chạy khỏi trận chiến, nhiều người ngã xuống và chết. Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than con trai vua cũng đã chết."
vi.R: Đa-vít hỏi: "Việc gì đã xảy ra? Hãy kể cho ta nghe." Người ấy đáp: "Quân ta đã bỏ chạy khỏi trận chiến. Nhiều binh lính đã bị giết. Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than con trai vua cũng đã chết."

ru.L: И сказал ему Давид: «Каково было дело? Расскажи же мне.» И он сказал: «Бежал народ с битвы, и также многие из народа пали и умерли, и также Саул и Ионафан, его сын, умерли.»

ja.L: そしてダビデは彼に言った。「事はどうなったのか？どうか、わたしに話してくれ。」彼は言った。「民は戦いから逃げ、また民の多くが倒れて死にました。そしてサウルとその子ヨナタンも死にました。」

uk.L: І сказав йому Давид: «Що сталося? Розкажи мені, прошу.» І сказав він: «Утік народ з битви, і також багато з народу полягло й померло, і також Саул і Йонатан, його син, померли.»

decisions.reason: "Word" here means a matter or event, as when Eli asked the runner from Aphek the same question (1 Samuel 4:16).

decisions.reason: The word for people often means the fighting men of Israel when they are at war (1 Samuel 4:3-4; 14:15).

decisions.choice: the report builds to its worst news: rout, many dead, and then Saul and Jonathan
decisions.reason: Each clause begins with "and also", so the news grows heavier step by step and ends with the deaths that matter most to David: the king and David's close friend.

decisions.reason: As across Samuel and Kings, "the people" meaning an army is "the troops" at Balanced and "the army" or "the soldiers" at Readable (m2).

decisions.choice: the young man: a young man, perhaps a servant or soldier
decisions.reason: The word means a youth or young man and is often used of a servant or an attendant in war, such as an armor-bearer (1 Samuel 14:1). It does not say what his place in Saul's army was.

decisions.choice: How do you know?: David asks for proof
decisions.reason: David does not simply accept the report; he presses for how the man knows. The question opens the way to the man's own account of Saul's death in verses 6-10.

decisions.choice: o jovem
decisions.reason: The word means a young man, often a servant or a soldier, without saying which (m1); "jovem" keeps it as open as the Hebrew and as dignified as the scene. David says "você" to him, as a man in authority to a stranger; "o rapaz" of 1 Samuel 17:58 is kept for a boy.

decisions.choice: "若者" for na'ar at every level
decisions.reason: He may be a servant or soldier; "若者" keeps the open sense, as 1 Samuel 20:22 for 'elem and the English "young man".

decisions.choice: the man's account differs from the narrator's in 1 Samuel 31: he is most likely lying to win David's favor
alternatives: the man found Saul still alive after he fell on his sword and finished him
decisions.reason: 1 Samuel 31:3-5 says that Saul was badly wounded by archers and, when his armor-bearer would not kill him, fell on his own sword. This man says he found Saul leaning on his spear with the enemy closing in, and that he killed him at Saul's own request (verses 9-10). The narrator's account in 1 Samuel 31 is the one the book itself gives as what happened, and the man has an obvious motive: he brings Saul's crown to David and expects a reward. David later says as much: the man thought he was bringing good news, and David's answer was to have him killed (4:10). Some readers have tried to fit the two accounts together, supposing that Saul's fall on his sword did not kill him at once and that the Amalekite then finished him. The text does not say so, and nothing in 1 Samuel 31 leaves room for a second man.

decisions.choice: the chariots and the masters of horsemen: the Philistine chariot force and its horsemen
decisions.reason: "Masters of the horsemen" is a way of saying the horsemen themselves, the men in charge of the horses., the riders. In the narrator's account the men who reached Saul were archers (1 Samuel 31:3).

decisions.choice: and there was Saul ... while the chariots
decisions.reason: Hebrew uses "look" twice to put the listener at the scene. Balanced says it with "there was" and joins the second picture with "while"; Literal keeps both "look"s.

decisions.choice: the Amalekite's story in the passé composé and imperfect ("je me suis trouvé", "j'ai vu") at every level
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: His account (verses 6-10) is speech to David, and French speech tells a past event in the passé composé, as the style guide sets for stories told inside speech. The quotation opened here stays open until the end of verse 10.

decisions.choice: the cramp: some kind of seizure, agony or faintness
decisions.reason: The word is found only here, so its exact sense is not known. It seems to name a gripping pain or spasm, or perhaps the dizziness of a dying man. In any case Saul says he is in the grip of something that will not let him go but has not yet killed him.

decisions.choice: for all my life is still in me: I am still fully alive
decisions.reason: Saul's complaint is that he is dying but not yet dead. The words give his reason for asking to be killed: he cannot end his suffering himself and fears falling into the enemy's hands alive, as he feared in 1 Samuel 31:4.

decisions.choice: Stand over me and kill me: the request Saul made to his armor-bearer in 1 Samuel 31:4
decisions.reason: In the narrator's account Saul asked his armor-bearer to kill him and was refused. The man's story borrows that request and gives himself the part the armor-bearer refused (verse 6, m1).

decisions.choice: Come here
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "stand over me" asks: come and stand by me, close enough to strike.

decisions.choice: la crampe (L); une douleur atroce (B)
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here and its sense is uncertain (m1). Literal keeps the English Literal's "cramp"; Balanced says what it most likely was, a gripping agony.

decisions.choice: kiharusi
decisions.reason: The word is found only here (m1). Literal says "kiharusi" (a seizure, a stroke), Balanced "uchungu mkali" (sharp agony); neither claims to know its exact sense.

decisions.choice: "cơn quặn thắt" (L); "cơn đau đớn" (B); "đau đớn quá" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is found only here (meaning decision); Vietnamese names a gripping pain at every level, the sense the English follows.

decisions.choice: o espasmo (L); uma agonia (B)
decisions.reason: The word is found only here (m1). Literal says "espasmo", a gripping seizure, which keeps the sense the English "cramp" aims at without the trivial sound of "câimbra" in Portuguese; Balanced says "agonia", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "ऐंठन" (L); "घोर पीड़ा" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is rare and its exact sense uncertain: a cramp, agony or faintness (meaning m1). Literal takes "cramp" ("ऐंठन"), Balanced and Readable the general "agony", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "मेरे प्राण अब भी मुझमें अटके हैं"
decisions.reason: "अटके हैं" (are caught, linger) says in Hindi idiom that life has not yet left the body (meaning m2).

decisions.choice: "судорога" (Literal); "мука" (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The rare Hebrew word names some seizure or agony (meaning m1); Literal takes the concrete "cramp", Balanced the broader "agony", Readable says plainly that he is in pain.

decisions.choice: "激しい苦しみ" (L), "ひどい苦しみ" (B) for hashavats
decisions.reason: The word is rare and its sense uncertain (cramp, agony or faintness); a general word for agony does not commit to one.

records.literal_gloss: And I stood over him and killed him, for I knew that not he would live after his falling; and I took the crown that [was] on his head and [the] armlet that [was] on his arm, and I have brought them to my lord here.

en.L: And I stood over him and killed him, for I knew that he would not live after he had fallen. And I took the crown that [was] on his head and the armlet that [was] on his arm, and I have brought them here to my lord."
en.B: So I stood over him and put him to death, because I knew he could not live once he had fallen. Then I took the crown from his head and the band from his arm, and I have brought them here to my lord."

es.L: Y me puse sobre él y lo maté, porque sabía que no viviría después de haber caído. Y tomé la corona que [estaba] sobre su cabeza y el brazalete que [estaba] en su brazo, y los he traído aquí a mi señor».

es.R: Así que me puse junto a él y lo maté. Sabía que no podía vivir después de haber caído. Luego le quité la corona de la cabeza y la banda del brazo. Te los he traído aquí a ti, mi señor».

fr.R: Alors je me suis approché de lui et je l’ai tué. Je savais qu’il ne pouvait pas vivre après être tombé. Puis j’ai pris la couronne sur sa tête et le bracelet à son bras. Je te les ai apportés ici, mon seigneur. »

am.L: እኔም በላዩ ቆሜ ገደልኩት፤ ከወደቀ በኋላ በሕይወት እንደማይኖር አውቄ ነበርና። በራሱም ላይ የነበረውን ዘውድ፣ በክንዱም ላይ የነበረውን አምባር ወሰድኩ፤ ወደዚህም ወደ ጌታዬ አምጥቻቸዋለሁ።»
am.B: ስለዚህ በላዩ ቆሜ ገደልኩት፤ ከወደቀ በኋላ ሊተርፍ እንደማይችል አውቄ ነበርና። ከዚያም ከራሱ ላይ ዘውዱን፣ ከክንዱም ላይ አምባሩን ወስጄ ወደዚህ ወደ ጌታዬ አምጥቻቸዋለሁ።»
am.R: ስለዚህ በላዩ ቆሜ ገደልኩት። ከወደቀ በኋላ እንደማይተርፍ አውቄ ነበር። ከዚያም ዘውዱን ከራሱ፣ አምባሩን ከክንዱ ወሰድኩ። ጌታዬ ሆይ፣ ይኸው ለእርስዎ አምጥቻቸዋለሁ።»

hi.L: तब मैंने उसके ऊपर खड़े होकर उसे मार डाला, क्योंकि मैं जानता था कि गिर जाने के बाद वह जीवित न रहेगा। और जो मुकुट उसके सिर पर [था] और जो बाजूबंद उसकी बाँह पर [था], उन्हें मैंने ले लिया, और उन्हें यहाँ अपने स्वामी के पास ले आया हूँ।"
hi.B: इसलिए मैंने उसके ऊपर खड़े होकर उसे मार डाला, क्योंकि मैं जानता था कि गिर जाने के बाद वह बच नहीं सकता। फिर मैंने उसके सिर से मुकुट और उसकी बाँह से बाजूबंद ले लिया, और उन्हें यहाँ अपने स्वामी के पास ले आया हूँ।"
hi.R: इसलिए मैंने उसके ऊपर खड़े होकर उसे मार डाला। मैं जानता था कि गिर जाने के बाद वह बच नहीं सकता। फिर मैंने उसके सिर से मुकुट और उसकी बाँह से बाजूबंद उतार लिया। मेरे स्वामी, इन्हें मैं यहाँ आपके पास ले आया हूँ।"

ru.L: И я встал над ним и убил его, потому что знал, что он не будет жить после своего падения. И взял я венец, который [был] на его голове, и браслет, который [был] на его руке, и принёс их моему господину сюда.»
ru.B: Я встал над ним и убил его, потому что знал: упав, он уже не выживет. Потом я снял венец с его головы и браслет с его руки и принёс их сюда моему господину.»
ru.R: Тогда я встал над ним и убил его. Я знал, что, упав, он уже не выживет. Потом я снял венец с его головы и браслет с его руки. Я принёс их сюда тебе, мой господин.»

ja.L: そこでわたしは彼の上に立って、彼を殺しました。彼が倒れた後では生きられないと知っていたからです。そしてわたしは、彼の頭にあった冠と、腕にあった腕輪を取り、それらをここに、わたしの主人のもとに持って来ました。」
ja.B: それで、わたしはそばに立って、とどめを刺しました。倒れたからには、もう生きられないとわかっていたからです。そして、頭の冠と腕の腕輪を取り、ここに、ご主人さまのもとにお持ちしました。」
ja.R: それで、わたしはそばに立って、サウルを殺しました。倒れてしまったので、もう助からないとわかったからです。それから、頭から冠を、腕から腕輪を取りました。それを、ご主人さま、あなたのところにお持ちしたのです。」

uk.L: І я став над ним і вбив його, бо я знав, що він не буде жити після свого падіння. І взяв я вінець, що [був] на його голові, і браслет, що [був] на його руці, і приніс їх сюди моєму панові.»
uk.B: Тож я став над ним і вбив його, бо знав, що він не виживе, раз уже впав. Потім я взяв вінець з його голови й браслет з його руки, і я приніс їх сюди моєму панові.»
uk.R: Тож я став над ним і вбив його. Я знав, що він не виживе після того, як упав. Потім я взяв вінець з його голови й браслет з його руки. Я приніс їх сюди тобі, мій пане.»

decisions.choice: after he had fallen: after he had been struck down in the battle
decisions.reason: "Fall" is the common word for dying or being struck down in battle; the lament uses it again and again (verses 19, 25, 27). The man means that Saul was already wounded beyond saving.

decisions.choice: the crown and the armlet: the marks of Saul's kingship
decisions.reason: The crown was probably a band or diadem worn as a sign of royal office (2 Kings 11:12). The armlet was a band worn on the upper arm. By bringing them to David the man is handing him the signs of the kingdom, and he expects to be rewarded for it (4:10).

decisions.choice: my lord: a title of respect for a superior, here for a king
decisions.reason: The man speaks to David as a subject speaks to his king (verse 2, m2).

decisions.choice: the band; you, my master
decisions.reason: Readable says "band" for the armlet and turns "my lord" into a direct address.

decisions.choice: le bracelet; mon seigneur (every level)
decisions.reason: "Bracelet" is the ordinary French word for a band worn on the arm. "Mon seigneur" is kept at Readable as well, where the English says "my master", because French "seigneur" is the plain word for a subject's lord and fits the Samuel note's "mon seigneur le roi".

decisions.choice: "mi señor" (L, B); "a ti, mi señor" (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole of 2 Samuel, as the Samuel terms note sets: one person is addressed with "tú", the king included, and respect is carried by "mi señor", "mi señor el rey" and "tu siervo"; Spanish never uses "usted" here.

decisions.choice: kikuku
decisions.reason: "Kikuku" is a band of metal worn on the arm or leg, closer to a warrior's armlet than "bangili" (a bracelet).

decisions.choice: "chúa tôi" (L, B); "ngài, thưa chủ" (R) for "my lord"
decisions.reason: The man speaks to David as a subject to a ruler (meaning decision); "chúa tôi" is the terms note's form for *adoni*, and Readable turns it into direct address, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "내 주" (my lord) at Literal and Balanced; "주인님" at Readable
decisions.reason: The man honors David as a superior; Korean "내 주" keeps the Hebrew title, and Readable uses the plain respectful "주인님", as the English Readable says "my master".

decisions.choice: o meu senhor (L, B); o senhor (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: people speak up to David as their lord or king with "o senhor", "meu senhor", "meu senhor, o rei", and the courtly "o seu servo" where the Hebrew has it, as 1 Samuel does for Saul (m3); David, like any king, answers his subjects with "você" and "vocês". Literal and Balanced keep the third person "o meu senhor" of the Hebrew; Readable turns it into the direct address "o senhor", as the English Readable says "you, my master". God speaks to David with "tu", and David prays with "tu".

decisions.choice: the young man to David: "ወደ ጌታዬ" in the third person (Literal, Balanced); "ጌታዬ ሆይ ... ለእርስዎ" (Readable)
decisions.reason: He bows to David as to a ruler and seeks his favour; the respectful "እርስዎ" fits his flattery where Readable turns the courtly third person into direct address.

decisions.choice: "बाजूबंद"
decisions.reason: An armlet worn on the upper arm, a royal ornament with the crown (meaning m2); "बाजूबंद" is the Hindi name for an ornament worn there, where "कड़ा" is a bracelet at the wrist.

decisions.choice: "अपने स्वामी" (L, B); "मेरे स्वामी ... आपके पास" (R)
decisions.reason: The man speaks of David in the third person as "my lord", the courtly form (meaning m3); Readable turns it into direct address with "आप", as the English Readable says "you, my master".

decisions.choice: "венец", "браслет"
decisions.reason: "Венец" for the royal diadem rather than "корона", which suggests a later European crown; the armlet is a band worn on the upper arm.

decisions.choice: "моему господину" in the third person (Literal, Balanced); "тебе, мой господин" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The man speaks to David in the courtly third person; Readable turns it to direct address as the English does. The address itself stays ты, as throughout 1 Samuel.

decisions.choice: adoni "わたしの主人" (L), "ご主人さま" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As Genesis and Numbers for adoni to a superior; David is not yet king, so "王さま" is not used.

decisions.choice: "腕輪" for the armlet
decisions.reason: The band worn on the upper arm, a mark of Saul's rank.

source.text: וַיַּחֲזֵ֥ק דָּוִ֛ד בִּבְגָדָ֖יו וַיִּקְרָעֵ֑ם וְגַ֥ם כָּל־הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And took hold David of his garments and tore them, and also all the men who [were] with him.

en.L: And David took hold of his clothes and tore them, and also all the men who [were] with him.
en.B: Then David took hold of his clothes and tore them, and so did all the men who were with him.
en.R: Then David took hold of his clothes and tore them to show his sorrow. All his men did the same.

es.L: Y tomó David sus vestidos y los rasgó, y también todos los hombres que [estaban] con él.
es.B: Entonces David se agarró la ropa y la rasgó, y lo mismo hicieron todos los hombres que estaban con él.
es.R: Entonces David se agarró la ropa y la rasgó en señal de dolor. Todos sus hombres hicieron lo mismo.

fr.L: Et David saisit ses vêtements et les déchira, et aussi tous les hommes qui [étaient] avec lui.
fr.B: Alors David saisit ses vêtements et les déchira, et tous les hommes qui étaient avec lui firent de même.
fr.R: Alors David a saisi ses vêtements et les a déchirés pour montrer son chagrin. Tous ses hommes ont fait la même chose.

sw.L: Daudi akashika mavazi yake akayararua, na pia watu wote waliokuwa pamoja naye.
sw.B: Ndipo Daudi akashika mavazi yake akayararua, na watu wote waliokuwa pamoja naye wakafanya vivyo hivyo.
sw.R: Ndipo Daudi akashika nguo zake akazirarua kuonyesha huzuni yake. Watu wake wote wakafanya vivyo hivyo.

vi.L: Đa-vít nắm lấy áo mình mà xé ra, và tất cả những người ở với ông cũng làm vậy.
vi.B: Bấy giờ Đa-vít nắm lấy áo mình mà xé ra, và tất cả những người đi theo ông cũng làm như vậy.
vi.R: Đa-vít liền nắm lấy áo mình mà xé ra để tỏ lòng đau buồn. Tất cả những người theo ông cũng làm như thế.

ko.L: 그러자 다윗이 자기 옷을 붙잡아 찢었고, 그와 함께 [있던] 모든 사람도 또한 [그렇게 했다].
ko.B: 그러자 다윗이 자기 옷을 움켜잡고 찢었다. 그와 함께 있던 모든 사람도 그렇게 했다.
ko.R: 그러자 다윗은 슬픔을 나타내려고 자기 옷을 잡아 찢었다. 다윗의 부하들도 모두 그렇게 했다.

pt.L: E Davi agarrou as suas roupas e as rasgou, e também todos os homens que [estavam] com ele.
pt.B: Então Davi pegou as suas roupas e as rasgou, e o mesmo fizeram todos os homens que estavam com ele.
pt.R: Então Davi pegou as próprias roupas e as rasgou, para mostrar a sua tristeza. Todos os homens dele fizeram o mesmo.

am.L: ዳዊትም ልብሱን ይዞ ቀደደው፤ ከእርሱም ጋር የነበሩት ሰዎች ሁሉ ደግሞ [እንዲሁ አደረጉ]።
am.B: ከዚያም ዳዊት ልብሱን ይዞ ቀደደ፤ ከእርሱም ጋር የነበሩት ሰዎች ሁሉ እንዲሁ አደረጉ።
am.R: ዳዊትም ሐዘኑን ለማሳየት ልብሱን ይዞ ቀደደ። ሰዎቹም ሁሉ እንዲሁ አደረጉ።

hi.L: तब दाऊद ने अपने वस्त्र पकड़कर फाड़े, और उसके साथ के सब पुरुषों ने भी [ऐसा ही किया]।
hi.B: तब दाऊद ने अपने वस्त्र पकड़कर फाड़ डाले, और उसके साथ के सब पुरुषों ने भी ऐसा ही किया।
hi.R: तब दाऊद ने अपना दुख दिखाने के लिए अपने कपड़े पकड़कर फाड़ डाले। उसके सब आदमियों ने भी ऐसा ही किया।

ru.L: И схватил Давид свою одежду и разорвал её, и также все люди, которые [были] с ним.
ru.B: Тогда Давид схватился за свою одежду и разорвал её. Так же поступили и все люди, которые были с ним.
ru.R: Тогда Давид схватился за свою одежду и разорвал её в знак горя. Все его люди сделали то же самое.

ja.L: そしてダビデは自分の衣をつかんで、それを裂いた。彼と共にいたすべての男たちも[そうした]。
ja.B: ダビデは自分の衣をつかんで裂いた。彼と共にいた者たちも皆、そうした。
ja.R: ダビデは、悲しみを表すために、自分の服をつかんで裂きました。部下たちも皆、同じようにしました。

uk.L: І схопив Давид свій одяг і роздер його, а також усі мужі, що [були] з ним.
uk.B: Тоді Давид схопив свій одяг і роздер його, і так само зробили всі мужі, що були з ним.
uk.R: Тоді Давид схопив свій одяг і роздер його на знак горя. Усі його люди зробили так само.

decisions.choice: tearing one's clothes: the act of a mourner
decisions.reason: Tearing the clothes was the first, sudden sign of grief at news of death or disaster (Genesis 37:34; Joshua 7:6). David does not rejoice that his pursuer is dead; he and his men mourn at once.

decisions.choice: his clothes
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text read "his garment" (one), and the form marked to be read aloud is "his garments". The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: to show his sorrow
decisions.reason: Readable adds what tearing the clothes meant (m1).

source.text: וַֽיִּסְפְּדוּ֙ וַיִּבְכּ֔וּ וַיָּצֻ֖מוּ עַד־הָעָ֑רֶב עַל־שָׁא֞וּל וְעַל־יְהוֹנָתָ֣ן בְּנ֗וֹ וְעַל־עַ֤ם יְהוָה֙ וְעַל־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֥י נָפְל֖וּ בֶּחָֽרֶב׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they mourned and wept and fasted until the evening for Saul and for Jonathan his son and for [the] people of Yahweh and for [the] house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.

en.L: And they mourned and wept and fasted until the evening for Saul and for Jonathan his son and for the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and for the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.
en.B: They mourned and wept and went without food until evening for Saul and his son Jonathan, for the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the house of Israel, since they had fallen by the sword.
en.R: They cried and mourned and did not eat until evening. They grieved for Saul and his son Jonathan, for the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and for the nation of Israel, because so many had been killed in battle.

es.L: Y se lamentaron y lloraron y ayunaron hasta la tarde por Saúl y por Jonatán su hijo y por el pueblo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y por la casa de Israel, porque habían caído a espada.
es.B: Hicieron duelo, lloraron y no comieron nada hasta la tarde por Saúl y su hijo Jonatán, por el pueblo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y por la casa de Israel, ya que habían caído a espada.
es.R: Lloraron e hicieron duelo, y no comieron hasta la tarde. Sintieron gran dolor por Saúl y su hijo Jonatán, por el pueblo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y por la nación de Israel, porque muchos habían muerto en la batalla.

fr.L: Et ils se lamentèrent, pleurèrent et jeûnèrent jusqu’au soir sur Saül et sur Jonathan son fils, et sur le peuple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et sur la maison d’Israël, parce qu’ils étaient tombés par l’épée.
fr.B: Ils se lamentèrent, pleurèrent et restèrent sans manger jusqu’au soir pour Saül et son fils Jonathan, pour le peuple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et pour la maison d’Israël, car ils étaient tombés par l’épée.
fr.R: Ils ont pleuré et se sont lamentés, et ils n’ont rien mangé jusqu’au soir. Ils étaient en deuil pour Saül et son fils Jonathan, pour le peuple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et pour la nation d’Israël, parce que tant d’hommes avaient été tués au combat.

sw.L: Wakaomboleza, wakalia, wakafunga mpaka jioni kwa ajili ya Sauli na kwa ajili ya Yonathani mwanawe, na kwa ajili ya watu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na kwa ajili ya nyumba ya Israeli, kwa sababu walikuwa wameanguka kwa upanga.
sw.B: Waliomboleza, wakalia, wakakaa bila kula mpaka jioni kwa ajili ya Sauli na mwanawe Yonathani, kwa ajili ya watu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na nyumba ya Israeli, kwa kuwa walikuwa wameanguka kwa upanga.
sw.R: Walilia na kuomboleza, wala hawakula chochote mpaka jioni. Waliwaombolezea Sauli na mwanawe Yonathani, watu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na taifa la Israeli, kwa sababu wengi walikuwa wameuawa vitani.

vi.L: Họ than khóc, kêu khóc và kiêng ăn cho đến chiều vì Sau-lơ, vì Giô-na-than con trai người, vì dân của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và vì nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên, bởi họ đã ngã xuống dưới lưỡi gươm.
vi.B: Họ than khóc, kêu khóc và nhịn ăn cho đến chiều vì Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than con trai người, vì dân của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên, vì họ đã ngã chết dưới lưỡi gươm.
vi.R: Họ khóc lóc, than thở và không ăn gì cho đến chiều. Họ thương tiếc Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than con trai người, thương tiếc dân của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và cả dân tộc Y-sơ-ra-ên, vì quá nhiều người đã bị giết trong trận chiến.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 사울과 그의 아들 요나단과 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 백성과 이스라엘 집을 위하여, 그들이 칼에 쓰러졌기 때문에, 저녁까지 슬퍼하며 울고 금식했다.
ko.B: 그들은 사울과 그의 아들 요나단을 위하여, 또 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 백성과 이스라엘 집안을 위하여 저녁까지 슬퍼하며 울고 금식했다. 그들이 칼에 쓰러졌기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그들은 울며 슬퍼했고, 저녁까지 아무것도 먹지 않았다. 그들은 사울과 그의 아들 요나단을 위해, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 백성을 위해, 이스라엘 민족을 위해 슬퍼했다. 많은 사람이 싸움터에서 죽었기 때문이다.

pt.L: E prantearam e choraram e jejuaram até a tarde por Saul e por Jônatas, o seu filho, e pelo povo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} e pela casa de Israel, porque tinham caído pela espada.
pt.B: Eles fizeram luto, choraram e ficaram sem comer até a tarde por Saul e pelo seu filho Jônatas, pelo povo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} e pela casa de Israel, porque tinham caído pela espada.
pt.R: Eles choraram, fizeram luto e não comeram nada até a tarde. Choravam por Saul e pelo seu filho Jônatas, pelo povo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} e pela nação de Israel, porque muitos tinham morrido na batalha.

am.L: አዘኑም፤ አለቀሱም፤ ስለ ሳኦልና ስለ ልጁ ስለ ዮናታን፣ ስለ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሕዝብና ስለ እስራኤል ቤት እስከ ማታ ድረስ ጾሙ፤ በሰይፍ ወድቀዋልና።
am.B: ስለ ሳኦልና ስለ ልጁ ስለ ዮናታን፣ ስለ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሕዝብና ስለ እስራኤል ቤት በሰይፍ ስለ ወደቁ አዘኑ፤ አለቀሱ፤ እስከ ማታም ምግብ ሳይቀምሱ ቆዩ።
am.R: አለቀሱ፤ አዘኑ፤ እስከ ማታም ምንም አልበሉም። ስለ ሳኦልና ስለ ልጁ ስለ ዮናታን፣ ስለ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሕዝብና ስለ እስራኤል ሕዝብ አዘኑ፤ ብዙዎች በጦርነት ተገድለው ነበርና።

hi.L: और वे शाऊल के लिए और उसके पुत्र योनातान के लिए और {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} की प्रजा के लिए और इस्राएल के घराने के लिए साँझ तक विलाप करते और रोते और उपवास करते रहे, क्योंकि वे तलवार से गिरे थे।
hi.B: वे शाऊल और उसके पुत्र योनातान के लिए, {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} की प्रजा और इस्राएल के घराने के लिए, साँझ तक विलाप करते और रोते रहे, और उन्होंने कुछ न खाया, क्योंकि वे तलवार से मारे गए थे।
hi.R: वे रोते और विलाप करते रहे, और शाम तक उन्होंने कुछ नहीं खाया। उन्होंने शाऊल और उसके पुत्र योनातान के लिए, {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} की प्रजा के लिए, और इस्राएल जाति के लिए शोक मनाया, क्योंकि युद्ध में बहुत से लोग मारे गए थे।

ru.L: И рыдали, и плакали, и постились до вечера о Сауле, и об Ионафане, его сыне, и о народе {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}, и о доме Израиля, потому что они пали от меча.
ru.B: Они скорбели, плакали и ничего не ели до вечера, оплакивая Саула и его сына Ионафана, народ {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}} и дом Израиля, потому что те пали от меча.
ru.R: Они плакали, горевали и ничего не ели до самого вечера. Они оплакивали Саула и его сына Ионафана, народ {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}} и весь Израиль, потому что так много людей погибло в битве.

ja.L: そして彼らは、サウルのため、その子ヨナタンのため、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の民のため、またイスラエルの家のために、嘆き、泣き、夕方まで断食した。彼らが剣に倒れたからである。
ja.B: 彼らは、サウルとその子ヨナタンのため、また{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の民とイスラエルの家のために、嘆き悲しんで泣き、夕方まで食を断った。彼らが剣に倒れたからである。
ja.R: 人々は泣いて悲しみ、夕方まで何も食べませんでした。サウルと息子のヨナタンのため、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の民のため、そしてイスラエルの国のために悲しんだのです。戦いで、とても多くの人が殺されたからです。

uk.L: І голосили, і плакали, і постили до вечора за Саулом, і за Йонатаном, його сином, і за народом {{divine_name:ГОСПОДНІМ|Ягве}}, і за домом Ізраїля, бо полягли вони від меча.
uk.B: Вони голосили, плакали й нічого не їли до вечора за Саулом і його сином Йонатаном, за народом {{divine_name:ГОСПОДНІМ|Ягве}} і за домом Ізраїля, бо ті полягли від меча.
uk.R: Вони плакали й голосили і нічого не їли до вечора. Вони сумували за Саулом і його сином Йонатаном, за народом {{divine_name:ГОСПОДНІМ|Ягве}} і за всім народом Ізраїля, бо так багато людей загинуло в битві.

decisions.choice: mourned, wept and fasted until evening: a day of public mourning
decisions.reason: Mourning was loud and public, and fasting until evening set the whole day apart for grief. The men of Jabesh-gilead fasted seven days for Saul (1 Samuel 31:13).

decisions.choice: the people of the LORD and the house of Israel: the same nation named twice
decisions.reason: Both phrases mean Israel, first as the people who belong to the LORD and then as one family descended from Israel. The mourning reaches beyond Saul and Jonathan to all who died in the defeat (verse 4).

decisions.choice: fallen by the sword: killed in battle
decisions.reason: "The sword" stands for war and violent death; it does not mean that every man died by a sword blow.

decisions.choice: went without food, did not eat; the nation of Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what fasting was. Readable says "the nation of Israel" for "the house of Israel" (m2) and "killed in battle" for "fallen by the sword" (m3).

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}: "le SEIGNEUR" in capitals, with the name "Yahvé" as the reader setting
decisions.reason: For the whole of 2 Samuel, as the Pentateuch and Samuel terms notes set: the divine name is "le SEIGNEUR", like the English "the LORD"; the span takes in the article and its contraction so that both options read naturally. "L'Éternel", the Segond tradition, is the alternative a reviewer may prefer.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}
decisions.reason: For the whole of 2 Samuel, as in the Spanish Pentateuch: the divine name is "el SEÑOR" in small capitals by default, like the English "the LORD", with "Yahvé" as the reader setting; the span takes in the article and its contraction ("del SEÑOR|de Yahvé", "al SEÑOR|a Yahvé").

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}
decisions.reason: Throughout 2 Samuel the divine name is BWANA in capitals, with "Yahwe" as the reader's alternative, as in the Pentateuch and Psalms.

decisions.choice: "kiêng ăn" (L); "nhịn ăn" (B); "không ăn gì" (R)
decisions.reason: "ăn chay" today means a meatless diet; the fast here was going without food, so Balanced and Readable say so plainly.

decisions.choice: The divine name is {{divine_name:주|야훼}} with the particle outside the span ("{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 백성")
decisions.reason: As the Korean style guide (section 7a) and the Samuel terms note: one particle fits both forms.

decisions.choice: prantearam
decisions.reason: "Prantear" is the Portuguese verb for mourning the dead aloud (m1) and takes the dead as its object; "lamentar" would also mean "regret". Balanced and Readable say "fizeram luto", the plain phrase.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}"
decisions.reason: The divine name takes the span used in every Hindi book of this translation; agreement with God is honorific plural in both options. Because Hindi "प्रभु" also renders Adonai ("Lord"), the setting is how a reader tells the two apart: with it on, only the divine name reads "याहवे".

decisions.choice: "उपवास किया" (L); "कुछ न खाया" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word for a fast; Balanced and Readable say what it meant, as the English "went without food" does.

decisions.choice: "постились" (Literal); "ничего не ели" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As the English, Balanced and Readable say what the fast was; Literal keeps the term.

decisions.choice: The persons mourned for come before the three verbs
decisions.reason: Japanese puts the object phrase before the verbs; the Hebrew list of verbs is kept whole.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד אֶל־הַנַּ֨עַר֙ הַמַּגִּ֣יד ל֔וֹ אֵ֥י מִזֶּ֖ה אָ֑תָּה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר בֶּן־אִ֛ישׁ גֵּ֥ר עֲמָלֵקִ֖י אָנֹֽכִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David to the young man who told to him, Where from this [are] you? And he said, [The] son of a man, a sojourner, an Amalekite I [am].

en.L: And David said to the young man who had told him, "Where [are] you from?" And he said, "I [am] the son of a sojourner, an Amalekite."
en.B: David said to the young man who had brought him the news, "Where are you from?" He answered, "I am the son of an outsider who lives among you, an Amalekite."
en.R: David asked the young man who had brought the news, "Where are you from?" He answered, "My father was an Amalekite who came to live in Israel."

es.L: Y dijo David al joven que le había informado: «¿De dónde [eres] tú?». Y él dijo: «Hijo de un inmigrante, un amalecita, [soy] yo».
es.B: David le preguntó al joven que le había traído la noticia: «¿De dónde eres?». Él respondió: «Soy hijo de un extranjero que vive aquí, un amalecita».
es.R: David le preguntó al joven que le había traído la noticia: «¿De dónde eres?». Él contestó: «Mi padre era un amalecita que vino a vivir a Israel».

fr.L: Et David dit au jeune homme qui l’avait renseigné : « D’où [es]-tu ? » Et il dit : « Je [suis] le fils d’un immigré, un Amalécite. »
fr.B: David dit au jeune homme qui lui avait apporté la nouvelle : « D’où es-tu ? » Il répondit : « Je suis le fils d’un étranger établi parmi vous, un Amalécite. »
fr.R: David a demandé au jeune homme qui avait apporté la nouvelle : « D’où es-tu ? » Il a répondu : « Mon père était un Amalécite venu vivre en Israël. »

sw.L: Daudi akamwambia yule kijana aliyempa habari, "Wewe [ni] wa wapi?" Akasema, "Mimi [ni] mwana wa mtu mgeni, Mwamaleki."
sw.B: Daudi akamwambia yule kijana aliyemletea habari, "Wewe ni wa wapi?" Akajibu, "Mimi ni mwana wa mgeni anayeishi kati yenu, Mwamaleki."
sw.R: Daudi akamwuliza yule kijana aliyemletea habari, "Wewe ni wa wapi?" Akajibu, "Baba yangu alikuwa Mwamaleki aliyekuja kuishi katika Israeli."

vi.L: Đa-vít hỏi người thanh niên đã báo tin cho mình: "Ngươi từ đâu đến?" Người ấy thưa: "Tôi là con trai của một ngoại kiều, một người A-ma-léc."
vi.B: Đa-vít hỏi người thanh niên đã đem tin đến: "Ngươi là người ở đâu?" Người ấy thưa: "Tôi là con của một người ngoại quốc sống giữa dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, một người A-ma-léc."
vi.R: Đa-vít hỏi người thanh niên đã báo tin: "Ngươi là người ở đâu?" Người ấy thưa: "Cha tôi là một người A-ma-léc đến sống ở Y-sơ-ra-ên."

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 자기에게 알려 준 젊은이에게 말했다. "너는 어디 [사람]이냐?" 그러자 그가 말했다. "저는 나그네의 아들, 아말렉 사람[입니다]."
ko.B: 다윗이 소식을 전한 젊은이에게 말했다. "너는 어디 사람이냐?" 그가 대답했다. "저는 이스라엘에 들어와 사는 이방 사람의 아들로, 아말렉 사람입니다."
ko.R: 다윗이 소식을 가져온 젊은이에게 물었다. "너는 어디 출신이냐?" 그가 대답했다. "제 아버지는 아말렉 사람인데, 이스라엘에 와서 살았습니다."

pt.L: E Davi disse ao jovem que lhe tinha contado: "De onde [é] você?" E ele disse: "Eu [sou] filho de um homem estrangeiro, um amalequita."
pt.B: Davi disse ao jovem que lhe tinha trazido a notícia: "De onde você é?" Ele respondeu: "Sou filho de um estrangeiro que vive entre vocês, um amalequita."
pt.R: Davi perguntou ao jovem que tinha trazido a notícia: "De onde você é?" Ele respondeu: "Meu pai era um amalequita que veio morar em Israel."

am.L: ዳዊትም ወሬውን የነገረውን ወጣት፦ «አንተ ከወዴት [ነህ]?» አለው። እርሱም፦ «እኔ የመጻተኛ ሰው ልጅ፣ አማሌቃዊ [ነኝ]» አለ።
am.B: ዳዊትም ወሬውን ያመጣለትን ወጣት፦ «ከየት ነህ?» አለው። እርሱም፦ «በመካከላችሁ የሚኖር የአንድ መጻተኛ ልጅ፣ አማሌቃዊ ነኝ» ብሎ መለሰ።
am.R: ዳዊትም ወሬውን ያመጣውን ወጣት፦ «ከየት ነህ?» ብሎ ጠየቀው። እርሱም፦ «አባቴ በእስራኤል ሊኖር የመጣ አማሌቃዊ ነው» ብሎ መለሰ።

hi.L: और दाऊद ने उस जवान से जिसने उसे बताया था, कहा, "तुम कहाँ के [हो]?" और उसने कहा, "मैं एक परदेशी पुरुष का पुत्र, एक अमालेकी [हूँ]।"
hi.B: दाऊद ने उस जवान से, जो उसके पास समाचार लाया था, कहा, "तुम कहाँ के हो?" उसने उत्तर दिया, "मैं एक ऐसे परदेशी का पुत्र हूँ जो आप लोगों के बीच रहता है, एक अमालेकी।"
hi.R: दाऊद ने उस जवान से, जो समाचार लाया था, पूछा, "तुम कहाँ के हो?" उसने उत्तर दिया, "मेरा पिता एक अमालेकी था जो इस्राएल में आकर बस गया था।"

ru.L: И сказал Давид юноше, который сообщил ему: «Откуда ты?» И он сказал: «Сын человека-пришельца, амаликитянина, я.»
ru.B: Давид спросил юношу, который принёс ему весть: «Откуда ты родом?» Тот ответил: «Я сын пришельца, амаликитянина, который живёт среди вас.»
ru.R: Давид спросил юношу, который принёс весть: «Откуда ты?» Тот ответил: «Мой отец — амаликитянин, который переселился в Израиль.»

ja.L: そしてダビデは、自分に知らせた若者に言った。「どこの者か？」彼は言った。「わたしは寄留者の息子、アマレク人です。」
ja.B: ダビデは、知らせを持って来た若者に言った。「どこの者か？」彼は答えた。「わたしは、あなたがたの中に身を寄せている寄留者の息子で、アマレク人です。」
ja.R: ダビデは、知らせを持って来た若者に聞きました。「どこの出身か？」若者は答えました。「わたしの父は、イスラエルに来て住みついたアマレク人です。」

uk.L: І сказав Давид юнакові, що розповів йому: «Звідки ти?» І сказав він: «Я син чоловіка-приходька, амаликитянина.»
uk.B: Давид спитав юнака, що приніс йому звістку: «Звідки ти?» Той відповів: «Я син приходька, що живе серед вас, амаликитянина.»
uk.R: Давид спитав юнака, що приніс звістку: «Звідки ти?» Він відповів: «Мій батько — амаликитянин, який прийшов жити в Ізраїлі.»

decisions.choice: the son of a sojourner: a man whose family had settled in Israel without belonging to it by birth
decisions.reason: A sojourner was someone living among Israel who was not an Israelite, under the protection of Israel's laws and bound by many of them (Leviticus 24:22; Numbers 15:15-16). So this man was no stranger to Israel's ways: he would have known who Saul was and what it meant to strike the LORD's anointed (verse 14).

decisions.choice: Where are you from?: a question about his people, not his route
decisions.reason: In verse 3 David asked where he had come from that day. Now he asks about the man himself, and the answer is his family and people. The question is the first step of a trial (verses 14-16).

decisions.choice: sojourner (Literal); an outsider who lives among you (Balanced); came to live in Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: As across these books, the word is "sojourner" at Literal and "outsider" at Balanced. Readable explains it as someone who came to live in Israel and makes the father the subject.

decisions.choice: un immigré (L); un étranger établi parmi vous (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is the one for a resident foreigner (m1), "l'étranger, l'immigré" in the Pentateuch terms list. Literal uses "immigré"; Balanced follows the English "an outsider who lives among you".

decisions.choice: "inmigrante" (L); "un extranjero que vive aquí" (B)
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch terms list for the ger: "inmigrante" at Literal, "extranjero" at Balanced, which says where he lives rather than "among you", since the man is speaking to David alone.

decisions.choice: mgeni (Literal); mgeni anayeishi kati yenu (Balanced); aliyekuja kuishi katika Israeli (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Mgeni" is the word for the sojourner (*ger*) set for the Pentateuch; Balanced adds that he lived among Israel and Readable explains it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "ngoại kiều" (L); "người ngoại quốc sống giữa dân Y-sơ-ra-ên" (B); "đến sống ở Y-sơ-ra-ên" (R)
decisions.reason: The sojourner is a foreigner settled among Israel (meaning decision); Balanced says who he was among, Readable makes the father the subject, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "나그네" (Literal); "이스라엘에 들어와 사는 이방 사람" (Balanced); a sentence about his father (Readable)
decisions.reason: The *ger* is a settled outsider, neither a passing traveller nor a citizen; Literal keeps the short Bible word, and Balanced says what it means, as the English levels do.

decisions.choice: estrangeiro (L); um estrangeiro que vive entre vocês (B); veio morar em Israel (R)
decisions.reason: "Estrangeiro" is the term of the Pentateuch in Portuguese for the ger, the outsider who lives under Israel's protection (m1); Balanced adds "que vive entre vocês", as the English "who lives among you", so that the word is not read as a passing traveller. Readable makes the father the subject, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "परदेशी"
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch term for the sojourner (ger), a foreigner settled in Israel (meaning m1); Balanced adds "who lives among you", as the English Balanced does.

decisions.choice: "пришелец" (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch note's word for the ger, a foreigner settled among Israel (meaning m1); Readable says what it means, as the English does.

decisions.choice: ger "寄留者" (L, B, Balanced with "あなたがたの中に身を寄せている"), Readable as a clause
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch form for ger; Readable explains it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "приходько" (L, B), as the shared note asks for the sojourner; Readable says it in a clause, as the English does
decisions.reason: A man settled in Israel without belonging to it by birth.
